newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Montreal sees fall in unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Montreal sees fall in unemployment.

text.p: The Bank of Montreal's chief economist Tim O'Neill said there are increasing signs the Canadian economy is starting to improve enough to push the unemployment rate below 10 percent.
O'Neill said Canadians opened up their pocketbooks in October spending 1.1 percent more on retail products in the month than in September.
He said the pickup in retail sales in October was led by solid gains in food, clothing, general merchandise and automotive products.
He said these numbers confirm that consumer spending is becoming more broadly based as a result of declines in interest rates.

Other signs of a rebounding economy included housing starts, which rebounded sharply in November, rising 17 percent to 138,200 and car sales, which rose strongly in October. Both housing starts and car sales show signs of improving in the coming months, O'Neill said.
He said the only weak link in the outlook for a strong domestic economy in Canada is soft employment growth. In November, only 7,000 new jobs were created.

"However, we remain confident that as interest-rate sensitive areas continue to strengthen, the labour market will start generating jobs that are needed to sustain a more broad-based recovery," O'Neill said.
"We expect this improvement to be evident as early as this month where employment should rise 0.2 percent to 0.3 percent and the unemployment rate could drop below 10 percent."
